import math
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

import pytest

from subject import compute_freshness_score


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_freshness_score_zero_days_old():
    now = datetime(2025, 1, 1, 12, 0, 0)
    created_at = now
    score = compute_freshness_score(created_at, now)
    assert score == 1.0


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_freshness_score_one_week_old():
    now = datetime(2025, 1, 8, 12, 0, 0)
    created_at = datetime(2025, 1, 1, 12, 0, 0)
    score = compute_freshness_score(created_at, now)
    expected = math.exp(-0.015 * 7)
    assert math.isclose(score, expected, rel_tol=1e-9)

    score = compute_freshness_score(created_at, now)
    expected = math.exp(-0.015 * 28)

def test_freshness_score_eight_weeks_old():
    now = datetime(2025, 2, 26, 12, 0, 0)

    score = compute_freshness_score(created_at, now)

@pytest.mark.unit
def test_freshness_score_future_created_at():
    now = datetime(2025, 1, 1, 12, 0, 0)
    created_at = datetime(2025, 1, 8, 12, 0, 0)  # one week in the future
    score = compute_freshness_score(created_at, now)
    # negative days_old becomes 0, so score should be 1.0
    assert score == 1.0


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_freshness_score_fractional_days():
    now = datetime(2025, 1, 1, 12, 0, 0)
    created_at = datetime(2025, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0)  # 12 hours earlier = 0.5 days
    score = compute_freshness_score(created_at, now)
    expected = math.exp(-0.015 * 0.5)
    assert math.isclose(score, expected, rel_tol=1e-9)


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_freshness_score_very_old():
    now = datetime(2025, 1, 1, 12, 0, 0)
    created_at = datetime(2000, 1, 1, 12, 0, 0)  # 25 years ago
    score = compute_freshness_score(created_at, now)
    days_old = (now - created_at).total_seconds() / 86400
    expected = math.exp(-0.015 * days_old)
    assert math.isclose(score, expected, rel_tol=1e-9)
    assert score > 0.0  # asymptotic to 0 but never negative
